business_scope.primary_industry_name: Maritime Seafarer Staffing and Vessel Crew Management Agency

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: OECD Multilateral Convention on Mutual Administrative Assistance in Tax Matters (extended to Gibraltar)
Gibraltar–UK Customs and Free Movement Agreements (2020 Brexit-effect provisions)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Proceeds of Crime Act 2015 (Gibraltar), as amended; Crime (Money Laundering and Proceeds) Act 2007 (Gibraltar), as amended; Financial Services Act 2019 (Gibraltar); Beneficial Ownership (Companies) Regulations 2018 (Gibraltar) made under Companies Act 2014; and Gibraltar Financial Services Commission (GFSC) AML/CFT Rules.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of passport (bio-data page) for all UBOs and directors
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public / competent police authority in country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Original utility bill or bank statement evidencing residential address (issued within last 3 months)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility provider / licensed bank in country of residence

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Professional reference letter from a licensed bank or law firm confirming overall legal and financial standing
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate banking institution or legal counsel
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization (non-Hague origin)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Corporate certificate of good standing for any corporate UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent Companies Registry of the corporate UBO's jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Draft or certified notified copy of the constitutional documents (Memorandum and Articles of Association / Trust deed) of each corporate UBO

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening against the UN Security Council Consolidated List, UK Consolidated List of Financial Sanctions, OFAC SDN List (for USD-clearing and correspondent banking), EU Consolidated List (as transplanted into UK law), Gibraltar's domestic sanctions registry and gazette, INTERPOL/Red Notices, and the GFSC's AML/CFT CDD rules. Enhanced due diligence is required for politically exposed persons (PEPs), including source of wealth verification, beneficial ownership structure education, ongoing transaction monitoring, and, where applicable, independent audit rights.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Gibraltar Companies Registry (GFSC e-Registry) – Registrar of Companies
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be in English and in Latin/Roman script. No mandatory phonetic transliteration is required; any non-English names must be submitted in English transliteration and are subject to the same credibility and obscenity tests. The use of Greek or Cyrillic characters or other non-Latin scripts is not permitted except where officially transliterated.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: An applicant may file a notice of appeal with the Registrar of Companies within 14 days of the rejection. The appeal must set out grounds for objection, together with any supporting consents from regulated ministries or authorities. The Registrar shall determine the appeal within 10 working days; if the name continues to be refused, the applicant may, within 28 days, petition the Gibraltar Supreme Court for judicial review under Part VI of the Companies Act. Frequently, a new name application may also be re-submitted with revised wording and additional consents.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office is accepted for registered office/service-of-process purposes when a licensed corporate service provider (CSP) acts as the in-country agent. However, the Gibraltar Maritime Administration requires a physical operational office within Gibraltar to satisfy the commercial-substance conditions of a Ship Crew Recruitment Agency licence under the Merchant Shipping (Maritime Labour Convention) Act 2013. Therefore, a virtual office alone is not sufficient for the licensed activity.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High – 70% of licensed crew recruitment agencies are subject to an unannounced inspection within the first 12 months of licensing, based on the Gibraltar Maritime Administration's inspection plan under the MLC 2006 and the Merchant Shipping (Maritime Labour Convention) Regulations 2013; inspections are also prompted by seafarer complaints and port-state control reports.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff (fixed by the Registrar of Companies under the Companies Act 2014)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Incorporation filing fee – standard exempted company (Memorandum and Articles of Association filing)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory incorporation fee under the Companies Act 2014; indexed by the Financial Services Commission

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO declaration registration (central beneficial ownership register)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory UBO filing fee under the Beneficial Ownership (Companies) Regulations 2018

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Licensed corporate service provider / registered agent services – year 1 (including AML/KYC checks, register maintenance, and nominee-vetted compliance)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for mid-cap transactional CSP services; typically GBP 1,250–1,500 for a 10-Act exempt company

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization and apostille processing – 5 interconnected documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Notary public and competently designated legalisation office (country of origin)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Notary tariff per certified page plus the $50 per-page Hague Apostille state fee (where applicable)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Preliminary regulatory assessment for Ship Crew Recruitment Agency (ISIC 5222) under the Gibraltar Maritime Administration
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Discretionary licence-eligibility assessment fee, refundable against the full crew supply licence fee

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 2014 (Gibraltar, Cap. 117) ss. 2, 30–51 (incorporation; memorandum and articles; statement of compliance; exemption from filing member list) and ss. 117–120 (registered office and officer registry); Merchant Shipping (Maritime Labour Convention) Regulations 2018, Reg. 1.4 (seafarer recruitment and placement licensing); Income Tax Act 2010 (non-resident tax exempt status); Employment Ordinance (Cap. 92).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Gibraltar Companies Registry — Registry of Companies, Civil Registry Department, H.M. Government of Gibraltar, 17 Secretary's Lane, Gibraltar GX11 1AA.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form 1 — Application for Registration of a Company, together with executed Memorandum and Articles of Association and s. 45 Statement of Compliance
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital exists for a Gibraltar exempted company (Cayman Exempted Company equivalence); one or more subscriber shares must be allotted. GMA licensing for crew recruitment requires documentary evidence of paid-up share capital or an irrevocable bank guarantee of not less than GIP 10,000 to cover seafarer wage liability under MLC 2006 Standards A1.4(5)(c) and A2.1(1)(e).
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTIONS OF THE FIRST MEETING OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF [COMPANY NAME] LIMITED (Gibraltar Exempted Company), held at the registered office, [date]: 1. The Company accepts the subscription of the initial subscriber shares and confirms the allotment to the founding member, fully or partly paid as ordered. 2. The registered office at [address], Gibraltar, is adopted and the Registered Office Service Provider, [CSP], is authorized to receive statutory notices. 3. [Director 1] and [Director 2] are appointed as Directors, [Name] as Company Secretary, and [Name] as Money Laundering Reporting Officer (MLRO). 4. Opening of bank accounts with [bank] is authorized, and the officers are delegated to apply for the Seafarer Recruitment and Placement Service License. Carried unanimously.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Gibraltar Companies Registry — Registry Online Services (ROS) portal, H.M. Government of Gibraltar
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name availability enquiry through the Registry Online Services (ROS) portal; reserve the proposed company name with the suffix 'Limited'; verify that the name is not identical or misleadingly similar to an existing registered name and that no prohibited expressions under s. 39 Companies Act 2014 appear; provide two alternative names to avoid rejection; obtain the name reservation confirmation letter.
required_dossiers: Proposed company name and two alternative names
Proof of residential address of the subscriber(s)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the requested name is queried for undesirability or conflict, amend the reservation request within 3 business days or appeal the Registrar's refusal to the Supreme Court of Gibraltar under s. 40(4) Companies Act 2014.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Memorandum and Articles Drafting and Notarization
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed Gibraltar Corporate Service Provider and Gibraltar Notary Public
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Engage a licensed Gibraltar Corporate Service Provider to prepare the Memorandum and Articles of Association in the statutory format; execute the exempted company declaration under s. 49 Companies Act 2014 so that the company qualifies as an exempted private company with non-resident ownership; have the subscriber signatures notarized by a Gibraltar Notary Public; arrange the registered office service agreement at a licensed CSP address.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Where drafting pages are defective, a notarial re-execution is required; any statutory inconsistency is cured by adopting restated Articles by unanimous written consent and filing the corrected version before formal submission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing and Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Gibraltar Companies Registry — Registry of Companies, Civil Registry Department
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File Form 1 with the executed Memorandum and Articles of Association, the s. 45 Statement of Compliance, and the consent of the registered office provider; pay the official state filing fee of USD 100 via SWIFT or local bank transfer; receive the Certificate of Incorporation with the Companies Registry number.
required_dossiers: Executed Memorandum and Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry raises a query, cure incomplete entries within 21 days under s. 48 Companies Act 2014; refile corrected forms via ROS and pay the GIP 25 deficiency correction fee; the date of incorporation is preserved only where corrections are completed before certificate issuance.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registered Office Adoption and Appointment of First Officers
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Gibraltar Companies Registry — Registry of Companies
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within 14 days of incorporation, file Form 4 (Notice of Registered Office, Directors, and Company Secretary) with the Registry; ensure the registered office is physically located in Gibraltar at licensed premises; appoint the first directors and the company secretary by board resolution; retain the signed consents and minutes in the statutory records book.
required_dossiers: Form 4 (Notice of Officers and Registered Office)
Consent and identity dossiers of directors
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Late filing is cured by paying the GIP 20 late-notification fee; if a director lacks qualification, file a replacement appointment and a corrective Form 4; the Registry accepts a consolidated correction by cover letter.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Exempted Company Status and Tax Exemption Confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Income Tax Office — Concessions and Rulings Unit, H.M. Government of Gibraltar
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the exempted company status confirmation with the Income Tax Office; provide a declaration of non-resident beneficial ownership; obtain the certificate of exempted company status and, where requested, a place-of-effective-management tax conclusion; attach all confirmations to the GMA licensing file.
required_dossiers: Passports and jurisdiction proof of ultimate owners
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Concessions and Rulings Unit requires supplementary information, provide an enhanced beneficial ownership structure chart; on refusal of exempt status, lodge an administrative appeal under the Income Tax Act 2010 (Gibraltar) within 30 days or relocate the locus of control.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Seafarer Recruitment and Placement Service License Application
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Gibraltar Maritime Administration (GMA) — Marine Labour Office, co-regulated by the Employment and Labour Standards Unit (Department of Employment)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the MLC 2006 crew agency licence application to the Gibraltar Maritime Administration on Form MLC-CREW-01 together with the manning policy, complaint handling procedure, bank guarantee evidence, and DBS vetting results; undergo an on-premise inspection by GMA officers; pay the annual supervision fee and obtain the Gibraltar Seafarer Recruitment and Placement Service License.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of Certificate of Incorporation
Evidence of paid-up capital or bank guarantee of GIP 10,000
DBS vetting certificates for recruiters and managers
Seafarer complaint handling and prevention procedure
Registered office and premises lease contract
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: On refusal, request a GMA reconsideration and appeal under the Merchant Shipping (Appeals) Regulations; licensing deficiencies can be cured by posting a compliance bond and implementing a remedial manning procedure endorsed by an approved Class Society surveyor within 10 business days.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Gibraltar Maritime Administration (GMA) — Marine Labour Office and Merchant Shipping Division; co-regulator: Employment and Labour Standards Unit (Department of Employment), H.M. Government of Gibraltar
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Gibraltar Seafarer Recruitment and Placement Service Licence (MLC 2006 Reg. 1.4.4) / Vessel Crew-Management Agency Operating Certificate (GMA-Form MLC-CREW-01)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Department of the Environment, Sustainability, Climate Change and Heritage (DESCC), H.M. Government of Gibraltar
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — Tier C (Schedule 2, Annex EIA-GIB-1) for non-polluting professional office activity; registration via Environmental Registration Form (ERF-1); no Full EIA Report required
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Zero industrial wastewater or VOC emissions; office discharge to municipal sewers compliant with the Water Services Ordinance (Gibraltar); office waste segregated per the Waste Management Ordinance (Gibraltar); WEEE routed to an approved recycler; crew recruitment electronic records stored in fireproof media cabinets; ambient noise limited to 40 dB(A) at the office envelope.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Certificate under the Fire Safety Act (Gibraltar) issued by the Gibraltar Fire and Rescue Service; annual fire risk assessment and evacuation drill record; structural load inspection certificate for filing and server rooms from the Building Control Unit of the Planning and Development Office; occupational clearance certificate from the Employment and Labour Standards Unit; DBS vetting of all crew-recruitment personnel; first-aid and workplace risk assessment under the Health and Safety at Work Act (Gibraltar).

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: HM Government of Gibraltar – Income Tax Office (ITO), Ministry of Finance; online filing via the ITO e-Returns portal and Companies House Gibraltar electronic registry. Gibraltar is a self-governing UK Overseas Territory with an autonomous tax administration; HMRC cooperation occurs only via UK/Gibraltar Exchange of Information and TIEA instruments.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: (1) Register the Cayman Exempted Company as an 'overseas company' with the Gibraltar Companies Registry within 30 days of establishing a registered office (Companies Act s.341), accompanied by certified Cayman incorporation documents and a Gibraltar-resident company secretary. (2) Apply to the Income Tax Office on Form TRO-1 for a Gibraltar Tax Reference Number (TRN), stating the business as ISIC 5222 crew manning. (3) Submit beneficial ownership particulars to the Gibraltar Financial Services Commission under the Beneficial Ownership (Companies) Regulations. (4) Obtain the seafarer recruitment agency licence from the Gibraltar Maritime Administration / Department of Employment before any crew payroll activity. (5) Register as an employer for PAYE and Social Security contributions and open a Gibraltar bank account for multi-currency payroll clearing.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Tax_Exempt_Zone – the Cayman Exempted Company is recognised as not subject to Gibraltar corporate profits, capital gains or withholding taxes provided its central management and control and any permanent establishment remain outside Gibraltar. If board meetings and crew payroll management are carried on in Gibraltar, the entity is reclassified as Entity_Level_Taxation and taxed on territorial income at the standard 12.5% (15% effective under Pillar Two for groups above EUR 750m revenue).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box election exists in Gibraltar; classification is determined by factual management/control. Available elections under the Income Tax Act include: (i) group relief election to surrender losses among Gibraltar-resident group members; (ii) election for GloBE safe-harbour treatment for qualifying MNE groups; and (iii) a territorial-scope notification election for foreign-source income derived from non-resident shipowners, submitted to the ITO with supporting payroll and invoicing records. Taxpayers may also elect the simplified deemed-profits basis for crew supply contracts where commercial accounts are unavailable.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT – not in force. Gibraltar is outside the UK VAT area; indirect taxation is limited to customs/excise duties on imported goods and a purchase tax on luxury retail. Services, including crew recruitment and payroll management, are outside the scope of VAT and no input tax recovery mechanism exists.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Not applicable – no VAT registration threshold. Employers must register for PAYE and Social Security at the first payment to crew members (no minimum turnover threshold); importers of physical goods require a customs registration for consignments above GIP 150 de minimis.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: None – Gibraltar does not mandate electronic invoicing, real-time fiscal clearance, API filing or digital stamping. Paper and PDF invoices satisfy the ITO record-keeping rules; monthly PAYE deductions must be filed electronically through the ITO e-returns portal by the 15th of the following month.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Structural not applicable – no VAT exists in Gibraltar, therefore no 0% export VAT rate or VAT refund mechanism applies to crew recruitment services. For income tax purposes, fees charged to non-resident shipowners for crew placement are treated as foreign-source only where recruitment, payroll and dispatch activities are performed and managed outside Gibraltar; if a Gibraltar office performs any part of the crewing value chain, the entire fee income is considered to accrue in Gibraltar and is taxable at 12.5% with no export exemption.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Gibraltar Single Administrative Document) – only for ancillary goods exports, not for crew services
Bill of Lading / Sea Waybill evidencing vessel and crew transit – retained for maritime labour licence inspections
Inward Remittance Certificate issued by a Gibraltar-licensed bank for foreign-currency crew management fees
Signed Crew Agency Service Agreement between the Cayman Exempted Co and the non-resident shipowner
MLC 2006 Crew List and Crewing Licence showing statutory compliance of the recruitment agency
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The ITO may open audit on the territorial-source filing within 6 years (extendable to 20 years for fraudulent failure); an unfounded claim of foreign-source treatment triggers assessment at 12.5%, late-payment interest at 8% per annum, and penalties up to 100% of the tax avoided plus GIP 100,000 per false return. The General Anti-Abuse Rule (Income Tax Amendment Act 2020) allows retrospective clawback of any tax advantage from artificial offshore structuring, and TIEAs with the UK/Cayman permit automatic exchange of the audit file.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of England (Sterling Monetary Authority and lender of last resort for GBP); Gibraltar Financial Services Commission (GFSC, the statutory banking and AML/CFT supervisor in Gibraltar under the Financial Services Act 2019); Government of Gibraltar (issuer of Gibraltar pound (GIP) notes and coin pursuant to the Currency Notes Act 1934, pegged at par with GBP); and the Cayman Islands Monetary Authority (CIMA) as the residual administrator of the Cayman Islands Exchange Control Regulations (1959), with the Cayman Islands dollar (KYD) pegged at USD 1 = 0.83333 KYD.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full current-account and capital-account convertibility exists throughout the United Kingdom, Gibraltar and the Cayman Islands; there are no exchange-control barriers to profit repatriation, dividend distribution, management-fee payments, payroll funding or repayment of shareholder loans routed through a Gibraltar treasury account of a Cayman Exempted Company to non-resident members. The Gibraltar pound is freely convertible into sterling at par without margin or delay; KYD is freely convertible into USD at the statutory peg. Practical hurdles are bank-level rather than statutory: (i) a Cayman offshore vehicle automatically attracts enhanced due diligence irrespective of the legitimate maritime staffing business; (ii) banks require demonstrable Gibraltar economic substance (registered office, resident director or controller, or licensed crewing presence) to avoid a shell-conduit classification; and (iii) each outward crew-wage payment must carry documentary transparency satisfying the flag-state maritime authority and the International Transport Workers' Federation (ITF). No Gibraltar or UK withholding tax, remittance fee, or prior regulatory approval is imposed on profit distribution, and no Bank of England consent is required for outward dividends.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory export-proceeds surrender obligation exists in the United Kingdom, Gibraltar or the Cayman Islands. Following the repeal of UK exchange controls in 1979 and the parallel liberalisation in Gibraltar and the Cayman Islands, all forced-sale and quota-based conversion mechanisms were eliminated. The group may retain 100% of crew-management fees, placement commissions and vessel-payroll funding indefinitely in any nominated currency (GBP, GIP, EUR, USD, PHP, INR); there is no 30-, 60- or 90-day repatriation timeline and no mandated conversion ratio into GIP/GBP or KYD/USD. Reporting obligations are limited to: (i) GFSC-licensed banks filing suspicious-activity reports and monitoring cash-intensive inbound flows; (ii) the company maintaining accurate Cayman annual-return and beneficial-ownership filings under the Cayman Companies Act and Beneficial Ownership Transparency Regulations; and (iii) external-statistics capture by the Bank of England when payments are made in sterling — none of which impose surrender, conversion or approval duties.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banco de Sabadell, S.A. - Gibraltar Branch

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Rating: High as a secondary disbursement and payroll rail; Low-to-Medium as the sole corporate treasury provider. GFSC-licensed Gibraltar electronic-money institutions under the Financial Services (Electronic Money) Regulations 2019 (notably PSI Pay) and FCA-authorised UK EMIs (Wise Business, Revolut Business, Airwallex, Ebury) will onboard a Cayman Exempted Company, provided the company supplies a GFSC-style EDD file containing a natural-person UBO, apostilled Cayman incorporation extracts, and a Gibraltar-licensed agent or registered-office appointment. Legal constraints: (i) EMIs are not credit institutions and cannot offer GIP/GBP Faster Payments or CHAPS settlement, with safeguarding limits typically restricting pooled balances to GBP/EUR 85,000; (ii) Revolut Business and Wise Business frequently decline Cayman-incorporated entities unless third-country economic-substance evidence is filed; (iii) an EMI cannot satisfy an MLC 2006 A1.4 crewing-licence auditor's requirement that payroll funds be segregated through a full-reserve regulated credit institution; and (iv) outbound seafarer wages to the Philippines, India and Indonesia demand SWIFT MT103 counterparties, which EMIs route through sponsor banks at higher cost and slower confirmation. Any EMI selected must be wholly owned and regulated in Gibraltar (GFSC) or the United Kingdom (FCA); use of an unregulated third-country EMI is inadvisable and may breach the Gibraltar AML/CFT Handbook.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Neither Gibraltar nor UK law imposes a compulsory physical board appearance. GFSC practice permits a remote video KYC interview with live document sharing (Teams or Zoom) where the Cayman entity is introduced by a GFSC-authorised lawyer, accountant or licensed corporate service provider, and a Gibraltar-resident company secretary or director is in place. Banco de Sabadell Gibraltar and Gibraltar International Bank accept fully remote onboarding for a Low_Risk_Standard maritime staffing agency, subject to a video call attended by both directors and the ultimate beneficial owner, plus a notarised apostille package from the Cayman General Registry evidencing incorporation, good standing, the register of members and the register of directors. NatWest International and CG Bank typically require at least one physical sign-off session at their Gibraltar office for the authorised signatories, or a manager's home-country visit where the UBO is an established shipowner or crewing principal. SG Kleinwort Hambros operates on a private-banking relationship mandate and mandates an in-person interview before account opening. In every case, certified true copies of passports, board resolutions, the Cayman register excerpts and the Gibraltar economic-substance file must be authenticated and held by the introducing regulated professional.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cayman Exempted Company with offshore-shell risk profile, nominee directorship and absence of a transparent UBO
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (i) current Cayman Certificate of Incorporation and Certificate of Good Standing (Apostille); (ii) full register of members and register of directors confirming no bearer shares (Cayman Companies Act, s. 43A); (iii) beneficial-ownership declaration filed under the Gibraltar Companies (Beneficial Ownership) Regulations 2019; (iv) a Gibraltar tax-residence or economic-substance attestation; and (v) a group-structure chart disclosing the natural-person UBO with 100% transparency to the GFSC-licensed bank.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Offshore vehicle lacking maritime-industry substance in the crew-staffing sector, causing payroll-flow and sanctions-scope ambiguity
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (i) Gibraltar-registered place of business with an appointed Gibraltar company secretary; (ii) crew-employment agreement templates endorsed with an ITF Blue Card or approved collective-bargaining agreement; (iii) managed-fleet list with vessel IMO numbers and ISM/ISPS Code certifications; (iv) at least one Cayman board director resident in Gibraltar or a Gibraltarian professional acting as controller; and (v) a Gibraltar office lease, payroll ledger and minimum-substance attestation evidencing real operational activity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trade-based money-laundering red flag where invoiced crew-management fees do not reconcile with declared vessel crew complement or wage scales
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (i) per-vessel crew manifests and seafarer employment contracts showing ITF-approved wage rates; (ii) a monthly payroll reconciliation statement matching aggregate declared wages against outward MT103 remittances to each named mariner; (iii) a crew-payroll run manifest signed by the crewing superintendent; (iv) independent verification from the flag-state registry or an ITF inspector; and (v) audited financial statements of the counterpart vessel-owner validating the agency-fee base.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions-screening failure on multi-jurisdiction crew payroll (Philippines, India, Indonesia, Eastern Europe) with partial-name matches on OFAC/EU/UN lists
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (i) real-time sanctions-screening output from a recognised engine (Refinitiv World-Check or Dow Jones) for every seafarer payee; (ii) a documented OFAC/EU/UN ownership-and-beneficiary analysis for each vessel owner, charterer and crewing principal; (iii) passport-page verification of each seafarer stored with the employment file; (iv) a negative-news and PEP-review trail covering state-owned crewing-source agencies; and (v) board attestation that no payments are routed to designated ports, sanctioned vessels, or flagged jurisdictions (Iran, North Korea, Russia, Syria, Crimea).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Potential breach of the Gibraltar Transfer of Funds (Information on the Payer) Regulations 2017 if remittance information is incomplete
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (i) every outward payment transmitted by SWIFT MT103 with fully populated beneficiary name and street-address fields, with no anonymous e-wallet disbursement; (ii) a documented beneficiary-identification audit file for each mariner; (iii) a transaction-monitoring register aligned with the GFSC Consolidated AML/CFT Guidance; (iv) bank-file proof that each seafarer wage account is held in the crew member's own name; and (v) an independent compliance-review opinion issued by a Gibraltar law firm confirming adherence to MLC 2006 and the ITF standard.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Shareholder equity or loan funding enters the Gibraltar operating account via SWIFT MT103 (ISO 20022 pacs.009.001.08) using external-purpose code SUBS for share subscriptions or INTE for intra-group loans, with the remitting bank verifying source of funds. The receiving GFSC-licensed bank requires a verification bundle comprising: (i) a certified board resolution authorising the share issue or loan (Cayman Companies Act, s. 45); (ii) an updated register of members and the relevant share certificates; (iii) the beneficial-ownership declaration filed under the Gibraltar Companies (Beneficial Ownership) Regulations 2019; (iv) a signed shareholder-loan agreement where the remittance is debt rather than equity; and (v) a Gibraltar tax-residence or economic-substance certificate to prevent shell-company classification. For amounts above GBP/EUR/USD 50,000, the bank applies a source-of-wealth backstop: audited group accounts, the UBO's personal tax returns, or asset-disposal contracts must be furnished. No Gibraltar Exchange Control permission or conversion ticket is required, and incoming funds remain in the remitted currency until redeployed for payroll or trade settlement.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Seafarer wages are settled by SWIFT MT103 with full beneficiary name and address under the information-on-the-payer rules, transmitted in USD, EUR, GBP, PHP, INR or IDR to each mariner's designated account. Low-value repetitive payroll is consolidated into a bulk ISO 20022 pain.001 file lodged by the treasury platform to the Gibraltar bank; high-value tranches above GBP 1 million are cleared through CHAPS via the London banking system. Vessel-supply and crew-change disbursements of material commercial value are effected under an irrevocable Commercial Letter of Credit (UCP 600) opened by a Gibraltar or UK clearing bank against the crewing agency's commercial invoice, the delivery certificate for crew services, and the Master's receipt; standby LCs secure the agency's payroll-prepayment obligations to the vessel owner. UK and EEA operating expenses settle through SEPA Credit Transfer or Faster Payments where VAT-compliant, but all cross-border payments to shipowners, manning principals and international seafarers remain MT103-based to preserve an unbroken audit trail for the flag-state maritime administration, the MLC 2006 licensing authority and the ITF.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright delivered forward foreign-exchange contracts in GIP/GBP, EUR and USD for crew-payroll and vessel-supply settlement exposures up to 12 months, executed on an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement or a Foreign Exchange Global Code-compliant execution venue.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) in PHP, INR, IDR, UAH and TRY, permissible only where the seafarer wage currency faces home-country convertibility restrictions and the notional exactly matches the underlying payroll exposure, booked through a GFSC-authorised MiFID II professional-client desk.

Cross-currency interest-rate swaps (CCIRS) converting a USD-denominated intra-group shareholder loan into a GIP/GBP floating-rate liability of the Gibraltar treasury vehicle, subject to board-approved hedge-policy documentation and derivative governance review.
GBP/EUR and GBP/USD rolling spot-forward swap structures for monthly wage-funding cash-flow management, provided the aggregate notional does not exceed 100% of projected 90-day payroll obligations.

European-style vanilla FX options (calls and puts) on EUR/USD and GBP/USD for protection against adverse payroll-cost movements in the crew nationalities' remittance corridors, purchased only with CRO sign-off and never used for speculative open positions.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return (Form 600) with updated register data
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 42 days after the anniversary of incorporation each year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of GBP 50 (USD 65) per month, doubling after 3 months; risk of administrative strike-off after 6 months of non-compliance.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Gibraltar Financial Services Commission (GFSC) via the Central Beneficial Ownership Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 31 January for the preceding calendar year; also required within 14 days of any UBO change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fixed penalty of GBP 50 (USD 65) per late filing, escalating to GBP 500 (USD 650) and potential criminal sanction for directors on prolonged default.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Tax Return (Exempt Company Nil Filing or Full Corporate Tax Return)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 30 November following the end of the tax year; extended to 31 January if electronically filed
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing interest of 4% per annum; penalties up to GBP 1,000 (USD 1,300) for non-filing; potential loss of exempt status.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Compulsory audit required unless the company qualifies as a 'small company': annual turnover ≤ GBP 2 million (USD 2.6 million), balance sheet total ≤ GBP 1 million (USD 1.3 million), and average employees ≤ 50. Exempted companies claiming non-resident status must file audited accounts if gross assets exceed GBP 100,000 (USD 130,000).
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) or UK-adopted IFRS (FRS 102) for small and medium-sized entities, in accordance with the Gibraltar Companies Act 2014.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Each year, the company must confirm the accuracy of its beneficial ownership (UBO) information with the Central Beneficial Ownership Registry. This confirmation must be signed by a director or secretary, and must verify all registers of members, directors, and PSCs. The annual confirmation is separate from any event-driven updates and is mandatory irrespective of whether shareholding transfers occurred.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 800 - USD 1,500 for Gibraltar registered office and corporate secretarial agent annual fee
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,500 - USD 8,500 for a small to medium-sized crew recruitment agency requiring a certified audit

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 12.5% (standard Gibraltar corporation tax on chargeable profits of a resident or Gibraltar-source non-resident company under the Income Tax Act 2010 as amended)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general statutory tax holiday; legacy 0% exempt-company regime abolished for accounting periods beginning on or after 1 January 2011. Effective rate for a Cayman Exempted Company structure is 0% on foreign-source crew recruitment and payroll fees not derived from Gibraltar sources; Patent/IP Box grants a 50% deduction on qualifying IP income yielding an effective 6.25% rate; no Gibraltar capital gains tax and no dividend/interest/royalty WHT.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 600 (Corporation Tax Return) filed with the Income Tax Office, Government of Gibraltar, through the eTax electronic filing portal; accompanying schedules submitted in XBRL or PDF via the same portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (one return per 12-month accounting period; no quarterly CIT instalments for exempted companies).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The Form 600 return and any balancing payment must be delivered within nine months of the end of the accounting period; for a 31 December year-end the deadline is 30 September of the following year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, Gibraltar tax reference (NREF) and registration number of the company.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Insert NR marker; enter the Gibraltar tax reference only where a Gibraltar-source income charge exists.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Place and country of incorporation and jurisdiction of tax residence (Cayman Islands exempted company status).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: State Cayman Islands; attach the Certificate of Non-Residence issued by the Commissioner if Gibraltar residence is disclaimed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting period start and end dates (DD/MM/YYYY).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Align to the 12-month period during which Gibraltar-source income is derived; file annually even with nil charge.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Principal business activity code and description (ISIC 5222: maritime seafarer staffing and vessel crew management agency).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Describe crew sourcing, manning, payroll, onboard welfare and client shipowner services; do not omit the activity class.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gibraltar-source trading income and gross commissions from crew placement.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include fees for crews supplied to Gibraltar-flagged vessels, Gibraltar-resident shipowners or gig-trade operations in Gibraltar territorial waters.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Foreign-source income excluded from the Gibraltar charge.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident exempted company: disclose foreign-source crew fees and charter management income outside the Gibraltar net; retain intercompany contracts.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Allowable deductions: seafarer salaries, payroll processing, licences, insurance, recruitment and administrative costs.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claims must be supported by Swift/Wire payment records and multi-currency payroll rails to actual seafarer accounts.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-trading income: interest, royalties, management fees received from associated shipowners.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident: report only Gibraltar-source non-trading items; apply statutory 0% WHT regime where payments pass through Gibraltar.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Related-party transaction disclosures and transfer pricing schedules.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose arm's-length pricing of crew placement fees with UK, EU and offshore shipowner associates; attach CUP/TNMM summary.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Loss relief utilised within the statutory carryforward window.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident company may offset only losses arising from Gibraltar-source trade; carryforward limited to 5 years.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total chargeable income after deductions and reliefs.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Compute strictly on Gibraltar-source income only for the non-resident exempted entity.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporation tax at 12.5% of chargeable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Nil charge where no Gibraltar-source income; otherwise apply 12.5%.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Credits, payments on account and any foreign-tax credits arising under the UK-Gibraltar DTA.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach TRC and DTA claim forms; no Gibraltar WHT credit exists on dividends, interest or royalties.
Refunds require verified bank routing and beneficial ownership declaration before disbursement.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration by director or authorised officer on truthfulness, completeness and substance of the return.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Directors of a Cayman Exempted Company structure sign personally; false declaration engages criminal liability.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: automatic penalty of GIP 1,500 plus daily surcharge of GIP 100 per day up to GIP 15,000; incorrect or fraudulent returns attract a tax-geared penalty up to 200% of undercharged tax; unpaid tax carries interest at 8% per annum; persistent default exposes directors to disqualification and criminal prosecution.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form ESR-1 (Annual Economic Substance Return) filed through the Gibraltar eTax portal with supporting substance evidence pack.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (submitted with the corporation tax filing cycle each accounting period).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within nine months of the end of the relevant accounting period, concurrent with Form 600.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Company identity and registered office in Gibraltar.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident exempted companies carrying on a relevant activity in Gibraltar must nonetheless file if the activity generates Gibraltar-source income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Relevant activity classification: shipping business or distribution and service centre business.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Classify seafarer and vessel crew management, payroll and manning services as service-centre or shipping activity; no reliance on Cayman exemption.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Core income generating activities (CIGA) performed in Gibraltar: strategic decision-making, crew sourcing, contract negotiation, payroll administration and compliance.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident: describe the physical performance of CIGA through Gibraltar staff and board meetings even where clients are foreign.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Employees, premises, operating expenditure and substance evidence.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach payroll records, lease agreements and board minutes; nil substance entries trigger an automatic ESR review.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: ESR non-compliance: fixed penalty of GIP 10,000 and continuing daily penalty of GIP 200 per day; automatic exchange of substance information with the UK and partner tax authorities; deregistration of the Gibraltar presence for persistent default.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% (Gibraltar imposes no withholding tax on dividend distributions; a Cayman Exempted Company may distribute profits free of Gibraltar dividend WHT, subject to ESR compliance).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke DTA relief, the non-resident shareholder or recipient must (1) obtain a Gibraltar Tax Residence Certificate (TRC) from the Commissioner of Income Tax where residence relief is claimed, or a TRC from the residence jurisdiction where the disbursing Gibraltar company is the payer; (2) file the prescribed DTA claim form with the Income Tax Office before or at the time of payment; (3) provide a beneficial ownership declaration and supporting share register/loan documentation; (4) retain evidence of substance (board minutes, CIGA records) for the UK-Gibraltar Double Taxation Arrangement 2019 application; processing is completed administratively within 30 business days where documentation is complete.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory: 0% WHT on IP royalties and 0% WHT on debt interest paid by Gibraltar companies to non-residents. Treaty (UK-Gibraltar DTA 2019): interest and royalties are chargeable only in the beneficial owner's residence state and are exempt at source in Gibraltar when paid at arm's length; standard 0% source-state rate applies without application of a supplementary domestic levy.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: GIP 10,000,000 aggregate related-party turnover per accounting period triggers the mandatory Local File; Master File is mandatory where the ultimate parent group reports consolidated annual revenue equal to or exceeding GIP 50,000,000; below these thresholds, a simplified contemporaneous transfer pricing disclosure is filed within Form 600 Box 8.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: The Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) apply fully to Gibraltar-resident companies and foreign companies operating in Gibraltar under the Income Tax (Substance Requirements) Regulations 2019 as amended. A ship crew recruitment agency engaged in crew sourcing, seafarer payroll, manning and vessel crew management carries on a relevant activity classified as shipping business or distribution and service centre business. The company must meet the CIGA test in Gibraltar: strategic and operational decisions, seafarer recruitment and contract negotiation, payroll execution and compliance management must be performed by adequate staff with premises and proportionate expenditure in Gibraltar. Annual filing on Form ESR-1 is mandatory; the evidential burden is on the company, and a Cayman Exempted Company structure cannot rely on foreign outsourcing arrangements to satisfy the substance test. Failure triggers penalties, automatic exchange of information to the UK and partner jurisdictions, and potential deregistration.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Corporate Income Tax Evasion and Fraudulent Misrepresentation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate recording of crew placement commissions in off-books accounts; processing seafarer wages through unregistered nominee bank accounts; backdated or fabricated crew contracts; omission of Gibraltar-source income from Form 600; mischaracterisation of foreign-source fees to avoid the 12.5% charge.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Civil penalty of up to 200% of the tax undercharged under the Income Tax Act 2010 as amended; interest at 8% per annum on the unpaid tax; criminal prosecution for fraudulent evasion with unlimited fines and imprisonment of up to 7 years on indictment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The corporate veil is pierced where directors sign false returns or direct the evasion; directors are jointly and severally liable for restitution of tax, penalties and costs; the court may impose travel bans, passport surrender, disqualification orders, and imprisonment for up to 7 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company and Economic Substance (ESR) Failure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining a Cayman Exempted Company shell in Gibraltar with no employees, no premises, no CIGA and no substance records; routing all crew recruitment and payroll functions through foreign service providers; undisclosed nominee directors concealing the true British or European shipowner principals.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fixed penalty of GIP 10,000 and continuing daily penalty of GIP 200 under the ESR Regulations; automatic exchange of substance information with the UK tax authorities and partner states; deregistration of the company under Gibraltar Companies Act powers for persistent non-compliance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors face personal daily fines for ongoing default, disqualification from acting as directors for up to 15 years, travel bans pending audit completion, and civil restitution orders for penalties incurred during their tenure.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Anti-Money Laundering and Sanctions Breach in Seafarer Payroll
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to conduct AML/KYC and source-of-funds checks on seafarers, shipowners and manning agents; disbursement of multi-currency payroll through pooled third-party or nominee accounts without beneficial ownership identification; payments to vessels, flag states or shipowners subject to international sanctions; operating a crew recruitment agency without the statutory licence required for ISIC 5222 maritime employment activity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal conviction under the Proceeds of Crime Act 2015 and the AML Regulations 2011 as amended: imprisonment up to 14 years and unlimited fines; freezing and forfeiture orders by the Gibraltar Sanctions Unit; withdrawal or refusal of the crew agency licence; inclusion on the public AML defaulters register.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are exposed to personal asset freezing, travel bans, extradition proceedings, disqualification for up to 15 years and civil recovery of tainted payroll funds under the Proceeds of Crime Act; personal criminal responsibility attaches where the director knowingly directed the payment flows.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Non-Compliance and Record Failure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to prepare contemporaneous Local File and Master File at the GIP 10,000,000 / GIP 50,000,000 thresholds; pricing crew placement fees to UK or EU shipowner affiliates without CUP or TNMM benchmarks; circular intercompany invoices shifting taxable profit from the Gibraltar operating entity to the Cayman exempted vehicle; undocumented management and charter fees.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Arm's-length adjustment of chargeable income by the Commissioner of Income Tax; penalty from 50% to 150% of the additional tax assessed; interest at 8% per annum computed from the original due date of the corporation tax return; public disclosure of the adjustment in serious cases.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who signed recklessly priced intercompany agreements may be personally assessed for the penalty portion; the court may issue travel bans pending resolution of the audit; deliberate destruction of transfer pricing records carries imprisonment of up to 2 years and personal civil restitution of the tax shortfall.
